<details markdown="1"><summary>How these forecasts were built and tested</summary>
<p>24 non-overlapping rolling-origin windows: the first 12 select the model and ensemble weights; the final 12 assess that frozen choice. Every fit uses only prices and matured training targets available at its origin. The unchanged-price forecast is retained unless validation MAE improves by at least 2%. Hyperparameters are fixed before testing. A current fit failure is explicitly labelled and falls back to no change.</p>
<p>ARIMA and damped exponential smoothing model log prices. AR(1)–GARCH with Student-t errors estimates the conditional return mean and volatility jointly: GARCH alone does not predict price direction. AI methods are Ridge, Extra Trees, gradient boosting and a small neural network; inputs are past returns, momentum and volatility, not an LLM or future news.</p>
<p>Each fit uses up to 630 past price observations or matured ML training examples. Fixed ML settings: Ridge penalty 50; 60 Extra Trees (depth 5); gradient boosting with 55 iterations; neural network with 24 and 12 hidden units. Feature and target scaling are fitted only on the training set. Unstable model forecasts implying more than a 100-fold weekly price change are rejected with a diagnostic, never clipped.</p>
<p>The central price is a back-transformed log-price estimate, not a guaranteed arithmetic mean. The displayed 90% range is calibrated from absolute rolling log-forecast errors; its coverage is approximate, not guaranteed. Illiquid unchanged quotes can make measured errors and ranges artificially small. Scheduled event dates are predictors; exact dividend/corporate-action price adjustments are not mechanically imposed. Unannounced earnings/news, spreads and execution prices remain outside these forecasts. NAV expenses are already embedded. Forecasts do not override the existing BUY / WAIT / HOLD / SELL rules.</p><p><strong>Cross-asset models:</strong> the three dependency models add lagged S&amp;P 500 USD returns, leave-one-out Baltic and fund return factors, and five peers selected by absolute correlation inside each trailing 252-observation training window. All external return series are delayed by two business days. Inputs include lagged returns, 5/7/20-observation averages, 7/20-observation volatility, 7-observation beta and trailing 7/60-observation correlations with the target. Correlation is a predictor, not a claim of causation. The same conservative lag is used in validation and live forecasts.</p><p>Dependency Ridge uses penalty 100; the tree models use the fixed settings above. Missing predictors are replaced by zero within the fitted pipeline; scaling and mature-target training use training data only. The current instrument universe is fixed, so survivorship bias remains possible. Historical fund NAV publication timestamps are unavailable; the two-day buffer is an assumption, not proof of historical execution availability. The original independent-model ensemble remains frozen; the added models compete individually using the first 12 windows. The final 12 windows evaluate the frozen choice.</p><p><strong>Seven-observation inputs:</strong> compounded and average return, SD, downside/upside deviation, Sharpe, Sortino, Omega, Calmar-style return/drawdown, empirical VaR/CVaR, drawdown, ulcer index, skewness, kurtosis, positive/unchanged-return fractions and autocorrelation. Ratios use zero risk-free return and zero minimum acceptable return; they are not annualised. With seven observations, empirical 95% CVaR reduces to the worst observation, so it is a noisy short-window feature, not a reliable tail-risk estimate. Undefined performance ratios have an explicit indicator and a neutral model placeholder.</p><p><strong>Calendar inputs:</strong> upcoming 1/7-business-day and recent 7-calendar-day counts by event type, plus weekday/month seasonality. Historical schedule dates are used only when the exact date is verified in a timestamped publication. Unverified schedules and the BLS macro calendar are available only from the current snapshot date; they are never backdated. The schedule is not exhaustive and uses event dates, not intraday release times; after-close announcements may affect the next trading session. An event date does not reveal an earnings surprise or guarantee a price direction. Event categories absent from training have no demonstrated learned effect. Predictors that were constant in every past usable feature row are held at their training value for the live neural forecast, preventing random neural responses to first-ever calendar inputs; this changes no historical validation/test input. The volatility proxy is shrunk halfway toward the training RMS baseline and bounded by the range of its training targets to prevent numerical extrapolation. Models also forecast realised variation using matured targets; conditional-scale-normalised residuals calibrate prediction ranges, with held-out coverage assessed separately.</p><p>Methods: <a href="https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/latest/univariate/forecasting.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">arch forecasting</a>; <a href="https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/applications/plot_time_series_lagged_features.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">time-series ML validation</a>.</p>
</details>
</details>

<details markdown="1"><summary>How these forecasts were built and tested</summary>
<p>24 non-overlapping rolling-origin windows: the first 12 select the model and ensemble weights; the final 12 assess that frozen choice. Every fit uses only prices and matured training targets available at its origin. The unchanged-price forecast is retained unless validation MAE improves by at least 2%. Hyperparameters are fixed before testing. A current fit failure is explicitly labelled and falls back to no change.</p>
<p>ARIMA and damped exponential smoothing model log prices. AR(1)–GARCH with Student-t errors estimates the conditional return mean and volatility jointly: GARCH alone does not predict price direction. AI methods are Ridge, Extra Trees, gradient boosting and a small neural network; inputs are past returns, momentum and volatility, not an LLM or future news.</p>
<p>Each fit uses up to 630 past price observations or matured ML training examples. Fixed ML settings: Ridge penalty 50; 60 Extra Trees (depth 5); gradient boosting with 55 iterations; neural network with 24 and 12 hidden units. Feature and target scaling are fitted only on the training set. Unstable model forecasts implying more than a 100-fold weekly price change are rejected with a diagnostic, never clipped.</p>
<p>The central price is a back-transformed log-price estimate, not a guaranteed arithmetic mean. The displayed 90% range is calibrated from absolute rolling log-forecast errors; its coverage is approximate, not guaranteed. Illiquid unchanged quotes can make measured errors and ranges artificially small. Scheduled event dates are predictors; exact dividend/corporate-action price adjustments are not mechanically imposed. Unannounced earnings/news, spreads and execution prices remain outside these forecasts. NAV expenses are already embedded. Forecasts do not override the existing BUY / WAIT / HOLD / SELL rules.</p><p><strong>Cross-asset models:</strong> the three dependency models add lagged S&amp;P 500 USD returns, leave-one-out Baltic and fund return factors, and five peers selected by absolute correlation inside each trailing 252-observation training window. All external return series are delayed by two business days. Inputs include lagged returns, 5/7/20-observation averages, 7/20-observation volatility, 7-observation beta and trailing 7/60-observation correlations with the target. Correlation is a predictor, not a claim of causation. The same conservative lag is used in validation and live forecasts.</p><p>Dependency Ridge uses penalty 100; the tree models use the fixed settings above. Missing predictors are replaced by zero within the fitted pipeline; scaling and mature-target training use training data only. The current instrument universe is fixed, so survivorship bias remains possible. Historical fund NAV publication timestamps are unavailable; the two-day buffer is an assumption, not proof of historical execution availability. The original independent-model ensemble remains frozen; the added models compete individually using the first 12 windows. The final 12 windows evaluate the frozen choice.</p><p><strong>Seven-observation inputs:</strong> compounded and average return, SD, downside/upside deviation, Sharpe, Sortino, Omega, Calmar-style return/drawdown, empirical VaR/CVaR, drawdown, ulcer index, skewness, kurtosis, positive/unchanged-return fractions and autocorrelation. Ratios use zero risk-free return and zero minimum acceptable return; they are not annualised. With seven observations, empirical 95% CVaR reduces to the worst observation, so it is a noisy short-window feature, not a reliable tail-risk estimate. Undefined performance ratios have an explicit indicator and a neutral model placeholder.</p><p><strong>Calendar inputs:</strong> upcoming 1/7-business-day and recent 7-calendar-day counts by event type, plus weekday/month seasonality. Historical schedule dates are used only when the exact date is verified in a timestamped publication. Unverified schedules and the BLS macro calendar are available only from the current snapshot date; they are never backdated. The schedule is not exhaustive and uses event dates, not intraday release times; after-close announcements may affect the next trading session. An event date does not reveal an earnings surprise or guarantee a price direction. Event categories absent from training have no demonstrated learned effect. Predictors that were constant in every past usable feature row are held at their training value for the live neural forecast, preventing random neural responses to first-ever calendar inputs; this changes no historical validation/test input. The volatility proxy is shrunk halfway toward the training RMS baseline and bounded by the range of its training targets to prevent numerical extrapolation. Models also forecast realised variation using matured targets; conditional-scale-normalised residuals calibrate prediction ranges, with held-out coverage assessed separately.</p><p>Methods: <a href="https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/latest/univariate/forecasting.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">arch forecasting</a>; <a href="https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/applications/plot_time_series_lagged_features.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">time-series ML validation</a>.</p>
</details>
</details>

<details markdown="1"><summary>How these forecasts were built and tested</summary>
<p>24 non-overlapping rolling-origin windows: the first 12 select the model and ensemble weights; the final 12 assess that frozen choice. Every fit uses only prices and matured training targets available at its origin. The unchanged-price forecast is retained unless validation MAE improves by at least 2%. Hyperparameters are fixed before testing. A current fit failure is explicitly labelled and falls back to no change.</p>
<p>ARIMA and damped exponential smoothing model log prices. AR(1)–GARCH with Student-t errors estimates the conditional return mean and volatility jointly: GARCH alone does not predict price direction. AI methods are Ridge, Extra Trees, gradient boosting and a small neural network; inputs are past returns, momentum and volatility, not an LLM or future news.</p>
<p>Each fit uses up to 630 past price observations or matured ML training examples. Fixed ML settings: Ridge penalty 50; 60 Extra Trees (depth 5); gradient boosting with 55 iterations; neural network with 24 and 12 hidden units. Feature and target scaling are fitted only on the training set. Unstable model forecasts implying more than a 100-fold weekly price change are rejected with a diagnostic, never clipped.</p>
<p>The central price is a back-transformed log-price estimate, not a guaranteed arithmetic mean. The displayed 90% range is calibrated from absolute rolling log-forecast errors; its coverage is approximate, not guaranteed. Illiquid unchanged quotes can make measured errors and ranges artificially small. Scheduled event dates are predictors; exact dividend/corporate-action price adjustments are not mechanically imposed. Unannounced earnings/news, spreads and execution prices remain outside these forecasts. NAV expenses are already embedded. Forecasts do not override the existing BUY / WAIT / HOLD / SELL rules.</p><p><strong>Cross-asset models:</strong> the three dependency models add lagged S&amp;P 500 USD returns, leave-one-out Baltic and fund return factors, and five peers selected by absolute correlation inside each trailing 252-observation training window. All external return series are delayed by two business days. Inputs include lagged returns, 5/7/20-observation averages, 7/20-observation volatility, 7-observation beta and trailing 7/60-observation correlations with the target. Correlation is a predictor, not a claim of causation. The same conservative lag is used in validation and live forecasts.</p><p>Dependency Ridge uses penalty 100; the tree models use the fixed settings above. Missing predictors are replaced by zero within the fitted pipeline; scaling and mature-target training use training data only. The current instrument universe is fixed, so survivorship bias remains possible. Historical fund NAV publication timestamps are unavailable; the two-day buffer is an assumption, not proof of historical execution availability. The original independent-model ensemble remains frozen; the added models compete individually using the first 12 windows. The final 12 windows evaluate the frozen choice.</p><p><strong>Seven-observation inputs:</strong> compounded and average return, SD, downside/upside deviation, Sharpe, Sortino, Omega, Calmar-style return/drawdown, empirical VaR/CVaR, drawdown, ulcer index, skewness, kurtosis, positive/unchanged-return fractions and autocorrelation. Ratios use zero risk-free return and zero minimum acceptable return; they are not annualised. With seven observations, empirical 95% CVaR reduces to the worst observation, so it is a noisy short-window feature, not a reliable tail-risk estimate. Undefined performance ratios have an explicit indicator and a neutral model placeholder.</p><p><strong>Calendar inputs:</strong> upcoming 1/7-business-day and recent 7-calendar-day counts by event type, plus weekday/month seasonality. Historical schedule dates are used only when the exact date is verified in a timestamped publication. Unverified schedules and the BLS macro calendar are available only from the current snapshot date; they are never backdated. The schedule is not exhaustive and uses event dates, not intraday release times; after-close announcements may affect the next trading session. An event date does not reveal an earnings surprise or guarantee a price direction. Event categories absent from training have no demonstrated learned effect. Predictors that were constant in every past usable feature row are held at their training value for the live neural forecast, preventing random neural responses to first-ever calendar inputs; this changes no historical validation/test input. The volatility proxy is shrunk halfway toward the training RMS baseline and bounded by the range of its training targets to prevent numerical extrapolation. Models also forecast realised variation using matured targets; conditional-scale-normalised residuals calibrate prediction ranges, with held-out coverage assessed separately.</p><p>Methods: <a href="https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/latest/univariate/forecasting.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">arch forecasting</a>; <a href="https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/applications/plot_time_series_lagged_features.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">time-series ML validation</a>.</p>
</details>
</details>

<details markdown="1"><summary>How these forecasts were built and tested</summary>
<p>24 non-overlapping rolling-origin windows: the first 12 select the model and ensemble weights; the final 12 assess that frozen choice. Every fit uses only prices and matured training targets available at its origin. The unchanged-price forecast is retained unless validation MAE improves by at least 2%. Hyperparameters are fixed before testing. A current fit failure is explicitly labelled and falls back to no change.</p>
<p>ARIMA and damped exponential smoothing model log prices. AR(1)–GARCH with Student-t errors estimates the conditional return mean and volatility jointly: GARCH alone does not predict price direction. AI methods are Ridge, Extra Trees, gradient boosting and a small neural network; inputs are past returns, momentum and volatility, not an LLM or future news.</p>
<p>Each fit uses up to 630 past price observations or matured ML training examples. Fixed ML settings: Ridge penalty 50; 60 Extra Trees (depth 5); gradient boosting with 55 iterations; neural network with 24 and 12 hidden units. Feature and target scaling are fitted only on the training set. Unstable model forecasts implying more than a 100-fold weekly price change are rejected with a diagnostic, never clipped.</p>
<p>The central price is a back-transformed log-price estimate, not a guaranteed arithmetic mean. The displayed 90% range is calibrated from absolute rolling log-forecast errors; its coverage is approximate, not guaranteed. Illiquid unchanged quotes can make measured errors and ranges artificially small. Scheduled event dates are predictors; exact dividend/corporate-action price adjustments are not mechanically imposed. Unannounced earnings/news, spreads and execution prices remain outside these forecasts. NAV expenses are already embedded. Forecasts do not override the existing BUY / WAIT / HOLD / SELL rules.</p><p><strong>Cross-asset models:</strong> the three dependency models add lagged S&amp;P 500 USD returns, leave-one-out Baltic and fund return factors, and five peers selected by absolute correlation inside each trailing 252-observation training window. All external return series are delayed by two business days. Inputs include lagged returns, 5/7/20-observation averages, 7/20-observation volatility, 7-observation beta and trailing 7/60-observation correlations with the target. Correlation is a predictor, not a claim of causation. The same conservative lag is used in validation and live forecasts.</p><p>Dependency Ridge uses penalty 100; the tree models use the fixed settings above. Missing predictors are replaced by zero within the fitted pipeline; scaling and mature-target training use training data only. The current instrument universe is fixed, so survivorship bias remains possible. Historical fund NAV publication timestamps are unavailable; the two-day buffer is an assumption, not proof of historical execution availability. The original independent-model ensemble remains frozen; the added models compete individually using the first 12 windows. The final 12 windows evaluate the frozen choice.</p><p><strong>Seven-observation inputs:</strong> compounded and average return, SD, downside/upside deviation, Sharpe, Sortino, Omega, Calmar-style return/drawdown, empirical VaR/CVaR, drawdown, ulcer index, skewness, kurtosis, positive/unchanged-return fractions and autocorrelation. Ratios use zero risk-free return and zero minimum acceptable return; they are not annualised. With seven observations, empirical 95% CVaR reduces to the worst observation, so it is a noisy short-window feature, not a reliable tail-risk estimate. Undefined performance ratios have an explicit indicator and a neutral model placeholder.</p><p><strong>Calendar inputs:</strong> upcoming 1/7-business-day and recent 7-calendar-day counts by event type, plus weekday/month seasonality. Historical schedule dates are used only when the exact date is verified in a timestamped publication. Unverified schedules and the BLS macro calendar are available only from the current snapshot date; they are never backdated. The schedule is not exhaustive and uses event dates, not intraday release times; after-close announcements may affect the next trading session. An event date does not reveal an earnings surprise or guarantee a price direction. Event categories absent from training have no demonstrated learned effect. Predictors that were constant in every past usable feature row are held at their training value for the live neural forecast, preventing random neural responses to first-ever calendar inputs; this changes no historical validation/test input. The volatility proxy is shrunk halfway toward the training RMS baseline and bounded by the range of its training targets to prevent numerical extrapolation. Models also forecast realised variation using matured targets; conditional-scale-normalised residuals calibrate prediction ranges, with held-out coverage assessed separately.</p><p>Methods: <a href="https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/latest/univariate/forecasting.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">arch forecasting</a>; <a href="https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/applications/plot_time_series_lagged_features.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">time-series ML validation</a>.</p>
</details>
</details>

<details markdown="1"><summary>How these forecasts were built and tested</summary>
<p>24 non-overlapping rolling-origin windows: the first 12 select the model and ensemble weights; the final 12 assess that frozen choice. Every fit uses only prices and matured training targets available at its origin. The unchanged-price forecast is retained unless validation MAE improves by at least 2%. Hyperparameters are fixed before testing. A current fit failure is explicitly labelled and falls back to no change.</p>
<p>ARIMA and damped exponential smoothing model log prices. AR(1)–GARCH with Student-t errors estimates the conditional return mean and volatility jointly: GARCH alone does not predict price direction. AI methods are Ridge, Extra Trees, gradient boosting and a small neural network; inputs are past returns, momentum and volatility, not an LLM or future news.</p>
<p>Each fit uses up to 630 past price observations or matured ML training examples. Fixed ML settings: Ridge penalty 50; 60 Extra Trees (depth 5); gradient boosting with 55 iterations; neural network with 24 and 12 hidden units. Feature and target scaling are fitted only on the training set. Unstable model forecasts implying more than a 100-fold weekly price change are rejected with a diagnostic, never clipped.</p>
<p>The central price is a back-transformed log-price estimate, not a guaranteed arithmetic mean. The displayed 90% range is calibrated from absolute rolling log-forecast errors; its coverage is approximate, not guaranteed. Illiquid unchanged quotes can make measured errors and ranges artificially small. Scheduled event dates are predictors; exact dividend/corporate-action price adjustments are not mechanically imposed. Unannounced earnings/news, spreads and execution prices remain outside these forecasts. NAV expenses are already embedded. Forecasts do not override the existing BUY / WAIT / HOLD / SELL rules.</p><p><strong>Cross-asset models:</strong> the three dependency models add lagged S&amp;P 500 USD returns, leave-one-out Baltic and fund return factors, and five peers selected by absolute correlation inside each trailing 252-observation training window. All external return series are delayed by two business days. Inputs include lagged returns, 5/7/20-observation averages, 7/20-observation volatility, 7-observation beta and trailing 7/60-observation correlations with the target. Correlation is a predictor, not a claim of causation. The same conservative lag is used in validation and live forecasts.</p><p>Dependency Ridge uses penalty 100; the tree models use the fixed settings above. Missing predictors are replaced by zero within the fitted pipeline; scaling and mature-target training use training data only. The current instrument universe is fixed, so survivorship bias remains possible. Historical fund NAV publication timestamps are unavailable; the two-day buffer is an assumption, not proof of historical execution availability. The original independent-model ensemble remains frozen; the added models compete individually using the first 12 windows. The final 12 windows evaluate the frozen choice.</p><p><strong>Seven-observation inputs:</strong> compounded and average return, SD, downside/upside deviation, Sharpe, Sortino, Omega, Calmar-style return/drawdown, empirical VaR/CVaR, drawdown, ulcer index, skewness, kurtosis, positive/unchanged-return fractions and autocorrelation. Ratios use zero risk-free return and zero minimum acceptable return; they are not annualised. With seven observations, empirical 95% CVaR reduces to the worst observation, so it is a noisy short-window feature, not a reliable tail-risk estimate. Undefined performance ratios have an explicit indicator and a neutral model placeholder.</p><p><strong>Calendar inputs:</strong> upcoming 1/7-business-day and recent 7-calendar-day counts by event type, plus weekday/month seasonality. Historical schedule dates are used only when the exact date is verified in a timestamped publication. Unverified schedules and the BLS macro calendar are available only from the current snapshot date; they are never backdated. The schedule is not exhaustive and uses event dates, not intraday release times; after-close announcements may affect the next trading session. An event date does not reveal an earnings surprise or guarantee a price direction. Event categories absent from training have no demonstrated learned effect. Predictors that were constant in every past usable feature row are held at their training value for the live neural forecast, preventing random neural responses to first-ever calendar inputs; this changes no historical validation/test input. The volatility proxy is shrunk halfway toward the training RMS baseline and bounded by the range of its training targets to prevent numerical extrapolation. Models also forecast realised variation using matured targets; conditional-scale-normalised residuals calibrate prediction ranges, with held-out coverage assessed separately.</p><p>Methods: <a href="https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/latest/univariate/forecasting.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">arch forecasting</a>; <a href="https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/applications/plot_time_series_lagged_features.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">time-series ML validation</a>.</p>
</details>
</details>

<details markdown="1"><summary>How these forecasts were built and tested</summary>
<p>24 non-overlapping rolling-origin windows: the first 12 select the model and ensemble weights; the final 12 assess that frozen choice. Every fit uses only prices and matured training targets available at its origin. The unchanged-price forecast is retained unless validation MAE improves by at least 2%. Hyperparameters are fixed before testing. A current fit failure is explicitly labelled and falls back to no change.</p>
<p>ARIMA and damped exponential smoothing model log prices. AR(1)–GARCH with Student-t errors estimates the conditional return mean and volatility jointly: GARCH alone does not predict price direction. AI methods are Ridge, Extra Trees, gradient boosting and a small neural network; inputs are past returns, momentum and volatility, not an LLM or future news.</p>
<p>Each fit uses up to 630 past price observations or matured ML training examples. Fixed ML settings: Ridge penalty 50; 60 Extra Trees (depth 5); gradient boosting with 55 iterations; neural network with 24 and 12 hidden units. Feature and target scaling are fitted only on the training set. Unstable model forecasts implying more than a 100-fold weekly price change are rejected with a diagnostic, never clipped.</p>
<p>The central price is a back-transformed log-price estimate, not a guaranteed arithmetic mean. The displayed 90% range is calibrated from absolute rolling log-forecast errors; its coverage is approximate, not guaranteed. Illiquid unchanged quotes can make measured errors and ranges artificially small. Scheduled event dates are predictors; exact dividend/corporate-action price adjustments are not mechanically imposed. Unannounced earnings/news, spreads and execution prices remain outside these forecasts. NAV expenses are already embedded. Forecasts do not override the existing BUY / WAIT / HOLD / SELL rules.</p><p><strong>Cross-asset models:</strong> the three dependency models add lagged S&amp;P 500 USD returns, leave-one-out Baltic and fund return factors, and five peers selected by absolute correlation inside each trailing 252-observation training window. All external return series are delayed by two business days. Inputs include lagged returns, 5/7/20-observation averages, 7/20-observation volatility, 7-observation beta and trailing 7/60-observation correlations with the target. Correlation is a predictor, not a claim of causation. The same conservative lag is used in validation and live forecasts.</p><p>Dependency Ridge uses penalty 100; the tree models use the fixed settings above. Missing predictors are replaced by zero within the fitted pipeline; scaling and mature-target training use training data only. The current instrument universe is fixed, so survivorship bias remains possible. Historical fund NAV publication timestamps are unavailable; the two-day buffer is an assumption, not proof of historical execution availability. The original independent-model ensemble remains frozen; the added models compete individually using the first 12 windows. The final 12 windows evaluate the frozen choice.</p><p><strong>Seven-observation inputs:</strong> compounded and average return, SD, downside/upside deviation, Sharpe, Sortino, Omega, Calmar-style return/drawdown, empirical VaR/CVaR, drawdown, ulcer index, skewness, kurtosis, positive/unchanged-return fractions and autocorrelation. Ratios use zero risk-free return and zero minimum acceptable return; they are not annualised. With seven observations, empirical 95% CVaR reduces to the worst observation, so it is a noisy short-window feature, not a reliable tail-risk estimate. Undefined performance ratios have an explicit indicator and a neutral model placeholder.</p><p><strong>Calendar inputs:</strong> upcoming 1/7-business-day and recent 7-calendar-day counts by event type, plus weekday/month seasonality. Historical schedule dates are used only when the exact date is verified in a timestamped publication. Unverified schedules and the BLS macro calendar are available only from the current snapshot date; they are never backdated. The schedule is not exhaustive and uses event dates, not intraday release times; after-close announcements may affect the next trading session. An event date does not reveal an earnings surprise or guarantee a price direction. Event categories absent from training have no demonstrated learned effect. Predictors that were constant in every past usable feature row are held at their training value for the live neural forecast, preventing random neural responses to first-ever calendar inputs; this changes no historical validation/test input. The volatility proxy is shrunk halfway toward the training RMS baseline and bounded by the range of its training targets to prevent numerical extrapolation. Models also forecast realised variation using matured targets; conditional-scale-normalised residuals calibrate prediction ranges, with held-out coverage assessed separately.</p><p>Methods: <a href="https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/latest/univariate/forecasting.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">arch forecasting</a>; <a href="https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/applications/plot_time_series_lagged_features.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">time-series ML validation</a>.</p>
</details>
</details>

HMM regimes are assigned only on exactly matching dates. Full and Last 126 retain all available return dates; regime columns omit dates without a common market label. Regime definitions use the full-history HMM fit and are descriptive, not an independent investment backtest.</p><p><strong>Path measures:</strong> drawdown, recovery and cumulative-return measures in regime columns use a synthetic sequence of the selected regime observations in chronological order, with other days omitted. <details markdown="1"><summary>How these forecasts were built and tested</summary>
<p>24 non-overlapping rolling-origin windows: the first 12 select the model and ensemble weights; the final 12 assess that frozen choice. Every fit uses only prices and matured training targets available at its origin. The unchanged-price forecast is retained unless validation MAE improves by at least 2%. Hyperparameters are fixed before testing. A current fit failure is explicitly labelled and falls back to no change.</p>
<p>ARIMA and damped exponential smoothing model log prices. AR(1)–GARCH with Student-t errors estimates the conditional return mean and volatility jointly: GARCH alone does not predict price direction. AI methods are Ridge, Extra Trees, gradient boosting and a small neural network; inputs are past returns, momentum and volatility, not an LLM or future news.</p>
<p>Each fit uses up to 630 past price observations or matured ML training examples. Fixed ML settings: Ridge penalty 50; 60 Extra Trees (depth 5); gradient boosting with 55 iterations; neural network with 24 and 12 hidden units. Feature and target scaling are fitted only on the training set. Unstable model forecasts implying more than a 100-fold weekly price change are rejected with a diagnostic, never clipped.</p>
<p>The central price is a back-transformed log-price estimate, not a guaranteed arithmetic mean. The displayed 90% range is calibrated from absolute rolling log-forecast errors; its coverage is approximate, not guaranteed. Illiquid unchanged quotes can make measured errors and ranges artificially small. Scheduled event dates are predictors; exact dividend/corporate-action price adjustments are not mechanically imposed. Unannounced earnings/news, spreads and execution prices remain outside these forecasts. NAV expenses are already embedded. Forecasts do not override the existing BUY / WAIT / HOLD / SELL rules.</p><p><strong>Cross-asset models:</strong> the three dependency models add lagged S&amp;P 500 USD returns, leave-one-out Baltic and fund return factors, and five peers selected by absolute correlation inside each trailing 252-observation training window. All external return series are delayed by two business days. Inputs include lagged returns, 5/7/20-observation averages, 7/20-observation volatility, 7-observation beta and trailing 7/60-observation correlations with the target. Correlation is a predictor, not a claim of causation. The same conservative lag is used in validation and live forecasts.</p><p>Dependency Ridge uses penalty 100; the tree models use the fixed settings above. Missing predictors are replaced by zero within the fitted pipeline; scaling and mature-target training use training data only. The current instrument universe is fixed, so survivorship bias remains possible. Historical fund NAV publication timestamps are unavailable; the two-day buffer is an assumption, not proof of historical execution availability. The original independent-model ensemble remains frozen; the added models compete individually using the first 12 windows. The final 12 windows evaluate the frozen choice.</p><p><strong>Seven-observation inputs:</strong> compounded and average return, SD, downside/upside deviation, Sharpe, Sortino, Omega, Calmar-style return/drawdown, empirical VaR/CVaR, drawdown, ulcer index, skewness, kurtosis, positive/unchanged-return fractions and autocorrelation. Ratios use zero risk-free return and zero minimum acceptable return; they are not annualised. With seven observations, empirical 95% CVaR reduces to the worst observation, so it is a noisy short-window feature, not a reliable tail-risk estimate. Undefined performance ratios have an explicit indicator and a neutral model placeholder.</p><p><strong>Calendar inputs:</strong> upcoming 1/7-business-day and recent 7-calendar-day counts by event type, plus weekday/month seasonality. Historical schedule dates are used only when the exact date is verified in a timestamped publication. Unverified schedules and the BLS macro calendar are available only from the current snapshot date; they are never backdated. The schedule is not exhaustive and uses event dates, not intraday release times; after-close announcements may affect the next trading session. An event date does not reveal an earnings surprise or guarantee a price direction. Event categories absent from training have no demonstrated learned effect. Predictors that were constant in every past usable feature row are held at their training value for the live neural forecast, preventing random neural responses to first-ever calendar inputs; this changes no historical validation/test input. The volatility proxy is shrunk halfway toward the training RMS baseline and bounded by the range of its training targets to prevent numerical extrapolation. Models also forecast realised variation using matured targets; conditional-scale-normalised residuals calibrate prediction ranges, with held-out coverage assessed separately.</p><p>Methods: <a href="https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/latest/univariate/forecasting.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">arch forecasting</a>; <a href="https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/applications/plot_time_series_lagged_features.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">time-series ML validation</a>.</p>
</details>
</details>

Regime definitions use the full-history HMM fit and are descriptive, not an independent investment backtest.</p><p><strong>Path measures:</strong> drawdown, recovery and cumulative-return measures in regime columns use a synthetic sequence of the selected regime observations in chronological order, with other days omitted. Benchmark measures use exact-date pairs with S&amp;P 500 USD price returns; currency and dividend bases differ.</p><p>— means the native R function is undefined for this sample, insufficient observations, or a missing benchmark; hover the cell for the specific reason. <p>Indicators are recomputed with TTR from the actual price history through the forecast origin plus only the scenario prefix through the recourse date. Bollinger SELL: price ≥ upper band; RSI SELL: RSI ≥ 70; Stochastic RSI SELL: smoothed %K ≥ 0.8; MACD SELL: MACD &lt; signal. Missing indicators cast no SELL vote.</p><p>2 of 1118 scenario–asset pairs authorise a recourse sale; 0 node–asset positions are actually reduced. A permission is not a mandatory trade.</p>

</details><details markdown="1" class=""><summary><strong>Mathematical model — no initial sales; gated recourse</strong></summary>
<div class="math-display">$$
\max_{q_0,c_0,\{q_{n(s)},c_s\}_{s=1}^{S}}\frac1S\sum_{s=1}^{S}\left[\frac{OUT_s(\mathcal R_s)-IN_s(\mathcal R_s)}{D}-P_s(q_{n(s)})\right].
$$</div><div class="math-display">$$
q_{i0}\ge q_i^{\mathrm{Current}},\quad c_0=B-\sum_i p_{i0}q_{i0}\ge0,\quad q_{i0},q_{in}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
$$</div><div class="math-display">$$
a_{is}=\mathbf1\{p_{iTs}<p_{i\tau s}\}\,\mathbf1\left\{\sum_{k=1}^{4}v^{\mathrm{SELL}}_{ik\tau s}\ge3\right\},\qquad
\bar a_{in}=\min_{s:n(s)=n}a_{is},\qquad q_{in}\ge(1-\bar a_{in})q_{i0}.
$$</div><div class="math-display">$$
c_s=c_0+\sum_i p_{i\tau s}(q_{i0}-q_{i,n(s)})\ge0,\quad
p_{0:\tau,s}=p_{0:\tau,s'}\Longrightarrow q_{n(s)}=q_{n(s')}.
$$</div><div class="math-display">$$
V_{ts}=\begin{cases}p_{ts}^{\mathsf T}q_0+c_0,&t\le\tau,\\p_{ts}^{\mathsf T}q_{n(s)}+c_s,&t>\tau,\end{cases}\quad
r_{ts}=\frac{V_{ts}}{V_{t-1,s}}-1,\quad
\mathcal R_s=\{H_t^{\mathsf T}w_s^{\mathrm{backcast}}\}_{t=1}^{N}\cup\{r_{1s},\ldots,r_{Ts}\}.
$$</div><div class="math-display">$$
w_{is}^{\mathrm{backcast}}=\frac{p_{i\tau s}q_{i,n(s)}}{p_{\tau s}^{\mathsf T}q_{n(s)}+c_s},\quad
2\le\sum_{i\in\mathcal F}\mathbf1\{q_{i0}>0\}\le4,\quad
2\le\sum_{i\in\mathcal F}\mathbf1\{q_{in}>0\}\le4.
$$</div><div class="math-display">$$
0\le q_{i0},q_{in}\le u_i,\quad
q_{i0},q_{in}\in\{0,10,11,\ldots\}\quad(i\text{ a new share}),\\
q_{i0}=0\ \text{or}\ p_{i0}q_{i0}\ge300,\quad
q_{in}=0\ \text{or}\ p_{i\tau s}q_{in}\ge300\quad(i\in\mathcal F,\ s:n(s)=n),\\
\frac{\sum_i\mu_i p_{i\tau s}q_{i,n(s)}}{\sum_i p_{i\tau s}q_{i,n(s)}}\ge\mu_{\mathrm{Current}}\quad(\forall s).
$$</div><div class="math-display">$$
P_s=0.00015\,n_{\mathrm{new},s}^{2}+\frac{0.001}{\sum_i\widetilde w_{is}^{2}}
+0.006\sum_{i\in\mathcal N_s}\left(\frac{(0.01-\widetilde w_{is})_+}{0.01}\right)^2\\
+0.006\sum_{\substack{i\in\mathcal E\\q_{i,n(s)}>0}}\frac{(10-q_{i,n(s)}d_i)_+}{10}
+0.002\sum_{\substack{i\in\mathcal E\\v_i>0}}\left(\frac{5q_{i,n(s)}}{v_i}\right)^2,
\qquad\widetilde w_{is}=\frac{p_{i\tau s}q_{i,n(s)}}{\sum_jp_{j\tau s}q_{j,n(s)}}.
$$</div><p>i indexes all eligible instruments; s indexes thirteen equiprobable joint forecast scenarios; n(s) is the information node identified only by the complete observed price prefix through τ = 2 (3 November); T = 5; B = EUR 15,000; D = 175. q is whole units, p is EUR price/NAV, c is nonnegative cash, H is the historical asset-return vector, and v with a SELL superscript is an individual indicator vote. If a = 0, sales are prohibited, including sales of units bought in stage one. If a = 1, a sale is permitted, not required. Identical observed prefixes share one decision; scenario labels and prices after τ do not determine the information node. The model uses forecast information for the remaining week at that node, never realised future observations.</p><p>𝓕 denotes funds, 𝓔 shares, 𝓝 newly introduced shares, d the historical five-year average annual cash dividend per unit, vᵢ the smaller of recent and median weekly traded volume, and uᵢ the audited unit cap. n_new counts newly introduced share positions; μ is the historical mean return. Shares with nonpositive historical individual netSD, excluded shares and shares failing the trading-activity rule cannot be increased: uᵢ = Current units. Otherwise uᵢ = max(Current units, floor(vᵢ/5)); NAV funds are volume-exempt. The penalty weights use invested-asset weights excluding cash, while historical-return backcast weights include cash in their denominator, matching the existing implementation. Each node order must satisfy cash feasibility, fund minima and gates in every scenario sharing that node. The same historical post-recourse backcast as the original model is retained explicitly; the historical block is not fixed at q₀. Fund expenses already enter NAV. Seven-thread neighbourhood search is heuristic; no global optimality certificate is claimed.</p>

Value of the stochastic solution and perfect information</strong></p><div class="table-wrap">

<table markdown="0"><thead><tr><th>Quantity</th><th>Penalised objective value</th><th>Expected netSD</th><th>Expected penalty</th><th>Meaning</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Existing saved policy</td><td>0.830230356</td><td>0.862857143</td><td>0.032626787</td><td>Active allocation; unchanged</td></tr><tr><td>EV</td><td>0.836173716</td><td>0.868571429</td><td>0.032397713</td><td>Optimise the elementwise mean price path; not comparable directly with RP</td></tr><tr><td>EEV</td><td>0.833737800</td><td>0.868571429</td><td>0.034833629</td><td>Fix EV first-stage units; optimise recourse on the original 13 scenarios</td></tr><tr><td>RP: diagnostic re-solve</td><td>0.834681751</td><td>0.868571429</td><td>0.033889677</td><td>Optimise the joint scenario problem, with common first-stage units</td></tr><tr><td>WS</td><td>0.838319376</td><td>0.868571429</td><td>0.030252053</td><td>Average of 13 separate perfect-information scenario optimisations</td></tr><tr><td>VSS = RP - EEV</td><td>0.000943952</td><td>—</td><td>—</td><td>Estimated value of modelling scenario uncertainty</td></tr><tr><td>EVPI = WS - RP</td><td>0.003637625</td><td>—</td><td>—</td><td>Estimated value of knowing the scenario before the first trade</td></tr></tbody></table>

</div><p>All values use the same EUR 15,000 budget, current holdings, no-sales rule, whole units,
liquidity caps, mean-return floor, two-to-four-fund requirement, reference universe, denominator 175 and existing penalty.
The 13 scenarios have equal probability. The deterministic EV problem uses the arithmetic mean of the joint price
paths; all comparison-asset forecast returns are rebuilt from that mean path. EV is not section 1.3.</p>
<div class="math-display">$$
\widehat{\mathrm{VSS}}=\widehat z_{RP}-\widehat z_{EEV},\qquad
\widehat{\mathrm{EVPI}}=\widehat z_{WS}-\widehat z_{RP}.
$$</div>
<p><strong>Objective-score units, not euros or expected-return percentages.</strong> The objective is netSD minus
the portfolio penalty. EEV fixes only the EV first-stage units; its second-stage decisions obey the original
information-node partition. WS lets the first-stage decision depend on the full future scenario, which is not
possible in actual trading.</p><p><strong>Solver limitation:</strong> these are heuristic estimates, not certified optimal VSS/EVPI. The same seven-thread integer neighbourhood search is used throughout. The existing saved policy scores 0.830230356; the diagnostic RP re-solve scores 0.834681751. The saved-policy gap against EEV is -0.003507444. A negative saved-policy gap reveals unfinished optimisation, not negative true VSS. The diagnostic re-solve is not substituted into the active trade tables.</p><p>The per-search iteration limit is 12. The following searches still improved at that limit: EEV, RP_refined, WS_02, WS_06, WS_08, WS_09, WS_12. The uncertainty from incomplete optimisation has not been quantified; differences must not be treated as precise economic values.</p><p><strong>What drives these estimates:</strong> EEV, RP and WS all average netSD 0.868571429. Their penalised-objective differences therefore come from the portfolio penalty, not an increase in average netSD. This is a comparison of these particular heuristic policies; it is not the VSS of a separately optimised unpenalised model.</p><p>Diagnostics computed: 2026-11-02T07:42:22.741451+00:00. Market prices and the active allocation were not refreshed by this calculation.</p><h4>How cross-asset dependence enters the scenarios</h4>
<p><strong>No mixing of forecasting methods between assets:</strong> scenario Gradient boosting uses the Gradient
boosting path for every eligible asset; the same applies to each of the 13 method labels. Validation ensemble is
an exception only in the sense that its asset-specific internal model weights can differ. Current inputs contain
no missing-method fallback paths.</p>
<p><strong>Historical dependence is retained:</strong> portfolio historical returns are calculated from aligned
same-date asset returns. The model does not shuffle individual asset observations. An explicit covariance matrix
is not a separate constraint or objective term in this netSD model.</p>
<p><strong>Forecast dependence is partial:</strong> Dependency Ridge, Dependency Extra Trees and Dependency Gradient
boosting include lagged market/fund factors, S&amp;P 500, five training-selected peers, trailing correlations and beta.
The selection uses up to 252 observations; inputs are lagged by two business days. However, the 13 joint scenarios
are model-output paths, not draws from a fitted joint return distribution. No correlated residual simulation,
copula, multivariate bootstrap or covariance-matching step is applied. Choosing the same method for all assets
does not by itself preserve their forecast correlation. These VSS/EVPI values therefore describe uncertainty
across forecasting methods, not all market uncertainty.</p>
<p>Definitions follow the maximisation convention in
<a href="https://mpi-sppy.readthedocs.io/en/latest/vss.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">mpi-sppy documentation</a>
and the <a href="https://ndcbe.github.io/optimization/notebooks/4/battery-forecasts-mpc/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Notre Dame stochastic-optimisation example</a>.
At exact optimality WS ≥ RP ≥ EEV; this ordering alone does not certify a heuristic result.</p></details><!-- INFORMATION_VALUE_END --><!-- FIRST_STAGE_AUDIT_START --><details markdown="1" id="first-stage-solutions" class="first-stage-solutions"><summary><strong>1.4.g. </div></details><details markdown="1"><summary><strong>1.4.g.d. Information timing: what is known now and what recourse means</strong></summary>
<p><strong>At the first decision:</strong> historical observations, current holdings, latest known prices/NAVs,
liquidity inputs, model forecasts and scenario probabilities are available. The realised future scenario is
unknown. One common q₀ is chosen for all scenarios. The forecasts already influence that choice through the
expected complete-policy objective; q₀ is not optimised on historical data alone.</p>
<p><strong>At recourse:</strong> the model allows additional purchases after 3 November, τ = 2 in the five-date
forecast grid. The simulated Current-portfolio change since the origin defines a down/flat/up node using ±0.1%.
Every scenario in the same node shares the same second-stage quantity vector. For the current inputs only flat
and up nodes occur. Forecast prices are used to simulate trading and wealth; no actual future observations
have been downloaded or used. The contingent decisions are planned today and would be executed only after
the corresponding information is observed. q₀ and all node-contingent second-stage quantities are optimised
jointly today; this is not a procedure that waits for actual future data and then reruns the optimiser.
This calculation is not a live receding-horizon trading system.</p><div style="max-width:100%;overflow-x:auto">

<table markdown="0" class=""><thead><tr><th>Node</th><th>Signal</th><th>Scenario count</th><th>Scenario labels</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>1</td><td>Flat</td><td>7</td><td>AR(1)-GARCH-t; Damped ETS; Dependency Extra Trees; Dependency Gradient boosting; Extra Trees; Gradient boosting; No change</td></tr><tr><td>2</td><td>Up</td><td>6</td><td>ARIMA(1,1,1); Dependency Ridge; Historical drift; Neural network MLP; Ridge regression; Validation ensemble</td></tr></tbody></table>

</div><div class="math-display">$$
c_0=B-p_0^{\mathsf T}q_0,\qquad
q_{n(s)}\ge q_0\ge q^{\mathrm{current}},\qquad
c_s=c_0+p_{\tau,s}^{\mathsf T}(q_0-q_{n(s)}).
$$</div>
<div class="math-display">$$
V_{t,s}=\begin{cases}
p_{t,s}^{\mathsf T}q_0+c_0,&t\le\tau,\\
p_{t,s}^{\mathsf T}q_{n(s)}+c_s,&t>\tau,
\end{cases}\qquad
r^{\mathrm{future}}_{t,s}=\frac{V_{t,s}}{V_{t-1,s}}-1.
$$</div>
<p>Here B = EUR 15,000; p₀ is the vector of latest known prices; pₜ,ₛ is the forecast price vector at date t in
scenario s; q₀ is the common first-stage holding; qₙ₍ₛ₎ is the post-recourse holding for the observed node;
c₀ and cₛ are cash before and after recourse. Purchases are self-financing and existing units cannot be sold.</p>
<p><strong>Important qualification — the implemented historical block:</strong> the optimisation does not append
forecast returns to a history fixed at q₀ weights. It backcasts the post-recourse portfolio through historical
asset returns, with weights marked at scenario-specific recourse prices:</p>
<div class="math-display">$$
w_{i,s}^{\mathrm{backcast}}=
\frac{p_{\tau,s,i}\,q_{n(s),i}}{p_{\tau,s}^{\mathsf T}q_{n(s)}+c_s},\qquad
r_{h,s}^{\mathrm{backcast}}=\sum_i H_{h,i}\,w_{i,s}^{\mathrm{backcast}}.
$$</div>
<div class="math-display">$$
z=\sum_{s=1}^{13}\frac1{13}\left[
\operatorname{netSD}\!\left(
(r_{1,s}^{\mathrm{backcast}},\ldots,r_{272,s}^{\mathrm{backcast}},
r_{1,s}^{\mathrm{future}},\ldots,r_{5,s}^{\mathrm{future}});\,\mathcal R_s
\right)-P(q_{n(s)},p_{\tau,s})\right].
$$</div>
<p>Hₕ,ᵢ is observed historical asset i return at date h; ℛₛ is the frozen comparison universe with that scenario's
forecast extension; P is the existing portfolio penalty. Cash has zero return. This is the objective actually
implemented and used for the reported VSS/EVPI estimates. Future decisions do not change observed H, but they
change the portfolio weights used to evaluate it. Thus the historical portfolio block is a hypothetical
scenario-dependent backcast, not the realised return history of holdings bought today.</p>
<p><strong>Consequences:</strong> first-stage and recourse decisions obey the information-node restrictions,
but it would be inaccurate to describe the full criterion as an immutable first-stage historical portfolio
plus only forward-looking recourse returns. The historical-only table above uses a separate fixed q₀ diagnostic,
with weights p₀,ᵢq₀,ᵢ/B, to make this distinction visible. No forecasting or optimisation rule has been silently
changed in this audit. If the intended criterion keeps historical portfolio weights fixed at the first-stage
decision, the backcast term must instead use p₀,ᵢq₀,ᵢ/B in every scenario. That would be a model change requiring
new optimisation and new VSS/EVPI calculations; it has not been applied here.</p></details><p>Sale is an archived unrestricted-sales diagnostic. Main and BothSignal, when present, use the new signal constraints and observed-prefix nodes. WS01–WS13 and VSS/EVPI remain the original no-sale experiments.</p></details><!-- FIRST_STAGE_AUDIT_END --><!-- STOCHASTIC_SALES_START --><details markdown="1" id="stochastic-sales" class="stochastic-sales"><summary><strong>1.4.h. Comparison: signal-gated sales allowed at both stages</strong></summary><p>Comparison: sales may also occur initially, but only when the current indicators give at least three SELL votes and the equally weighted terminal forecast is below the latest price. Recourse uses the same scenario-specific gate as the main policy. No shorting, borrowing or unconditional sale is allowed.</p><p>Expected netSD 0.902857; objective 0.883806; initial sales 0.</p><p><strong>Why this solution equals the main one:</strong> no currently held asset meets the initial sale condition. Comparison: no sales at either stage</strong></summary><p><strong>Comparison only:</strong> the frozen original policy prohibits sales at both stages and uses its original down/flat/up information nodes. It is no longer the main trade plan.</p><p><strong>Full-catalogue quantity search:</strong> all 86 history/forecast-eligible instruments (63 shares and 23 funds) are modelled; purchases remain subject to liquidity and minimum-lot rules. The decision quantities are searched directly, not chosen from five legacy portfolios. Seven threads evaluate integer moves. This nonconvex heuristic has no global-optimality certificate; the coverage table records proposals and feasible proposals for each variable.</p><p>Expected scenario netSD <strong>0.862857</strong>; expected penalty 0.032627; objective 0.830230. Historical first-stage netSD 0.862857 is a separate diagnostic. Every scenario contains 272 common historical returns (2025-10-01–2026-10-29) plus all five forecast dates, 2–6 November. The enlarged frozen reference system has denominator 175; older numerical scores from the smaller universe must not be substituted.</p><p>First-stage decisions are common to all scenarios. After 3 November, scenarios with the same observed Current-return node (below −0.1%, within ±0.1%, above +0.1%) share recourse quantities. No existing positions can be sold. The 15,000 EUR budget includes cash; later trades are self-financing. Two to four funds, whole units, minimum fund value EUR 300 and at least 10 units in new stock positions apply. The share liquidity rule is unchanged: typical weekly volume at least five times the total holding, at least 80% active sessions out of 65, and at least four out of the last five. MOLNR cannot be purchased.</p><p>Shares with nonpositive individual historical netSD cannot be increased; existing units are retained. RKB1R remains reference-only by the earlier explicit exclusion. Every offered fund with enough history is considered; there is no fixed three-fund basket or mandatory emerging-market allocation.</p>
<p>Target invested EUR 14,165.38; cash EUR 834.62; OUT / IN 151 / 0; netSD 0.862857. Average annual historical cash dividends EUR 429.26; embedded annual fund costs approximately EUR 9.00. Accumulating funds make no cash dividend payment.</p><h4>Table 1.4.i.a. First-stage holdings and purchases</h4>

<p>All eligible coordinates are proposed in the first stage and every observed recourse node. A proposal can fail the budget, fund count, minimum lot, liquidity or mean floor. No global optimum is claimed. Funds without enough observations and shares without usable histories are listed in the catalogue rather than silently discarded. Unavailable individual methods use an explicitly registered No change scenario path; this is not a claim that the failed method fitted.</p>

</details><details markdown="1" class=""><summary><strong>Mathematical model</strong></summary>
$$\max_{q,c_0,\{y_s,c_s\}}\frac1{13}\sum_s\left[\frac{OUT_s(q,y_s)-IN_s(q,y_s)}{175}-P_s(y_s)\right].$$
$$\sum_i p_{i0}q_i+c_0=15000,\quad c_s=c_0+\sum_i p_{is\tau}(q_i-y_{is})\ge0.$$
$$q_i\ge q_i^{Current},\quad y_{is}\ge q_i,\quad q_i,y_{is}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0},\quad g(s)=g(s')\Rightarrow y_{is}=y_{is'}.$$
$$\mathcal X_s=\{R^{hist}_{1s},\ldots,R^{hist}_{272,s},R_{s1},\ldots,R_{s5}\}.$$
<p>Asset index i runs across the complete forecast-eligible catalogue, not a preselected fund trio. Historical portfolio weights freeze the final allocation including cash; forecast returns follow the two-stage wealth path. Exact empirical dominance checks include TSD interior extrema and its mean condition. The original position-count, effective-count, small-stock-position and dividend penalties remain, plus the 0.002 squared liquidity-utilisation penalty. Recurring fund expenses already enter NAV returns. Execution delays, bid–ask spreads and taxes remain unmodelled.</p>
</details></details><!-- NO_SALE_BASELINE_END --></details><!-- STOCHASTIC_UPDATE3_END -->
<details markdown="1" class="report-section" id="analytics-1-3">
<summary><strong>1.5. Earnings outcomes and subsequent price changes</strong></summary>

Official announcement text allowed 197 of 326 earnings releases to be classified. Higher or lower profit refers to the issuer's explicit comparison with the earlier comparable period. In line or unchanged is used only for an explicit plan, forecast, expectation or unchanged-profit statement. Loss requires an explicit realised net or operating loss.

<!-- MARKET_ANALYSIS_START --><details markdown="1" id="analytics-2" class="analytics-group market-analysis"><summary><strong>2. Market analysis — Baltic and global HMM regimes</strong></summary><p><strong>External market regimes:</strong> five Baltic indices define local conditions and MSCI World defines global conditions. 4,817 common observations, 2007-01-04–2026-10-30. At the last common date the estimated regime is <strong>R1: both calm</strong>. This is a statistical volatility state, not a guarantee that prices will rise.</p><p>Market analysis is section 2; portfolio analysis follows in section 3. All market-model estimation uses R: <code>depmixS4</code> and <code>markovchain</code>. The resulting external regimes are ready for a subsequent market-conditioned scenario design; existing allocation quantities are not reoptimised in this market-identification step.</p><p><strong>Matrix stability check:</strong> first-order bootstrap p = 0.174; time-homogeneity bootstrap p = 0.002. The full-history matrix varies over time in the data and is presented as a historical summary. Recent-window comparisons and the implications for forecasting are in 2.7.</p><details markdown="1" id="market-analysis-1"><summary><strong>2.1. Data, index identities and observation calendar</strong></summary>

<p>Exact indices are used, not ETF proxies. MSCI World is the official index code 990100, EUR, gross total return (GRTR). OMXB10 is the requested price index; the other local indices are gross-return indices. </details><p>Identical duplicate Nasdaq endpoint rows and its non-observation previous-close chart anchor are removed. Conflicting duplicate closes cause a validation failure. No missing close is forward-filled. Log returns are calculated after taking the intersection of observed closing dates, so all indices cover the same intervals. One initial return is then removed for lagged regressors. A step is one common observation interval, which can span more than one calendar or exchange trading day.</p><p>Some individual series reach 2026-11-02, but Vilnius closes make 2026-10-30 the latest complete joint observation. The headline regime is dated accordingly. Local and global closes occur at different times; lagged market regressors avoid using the later same-day global close as a Baltic predictor.</p><details markdown="1"><summary><strong>Figure 2.a. Official index histories on a common EUR observation calendar</strong></summary>

</details><details markdown="1" id="market-analysis-2"><summary><strong>2.2. Two-state HMM specification and estimation</strong></summary>

<p>Two Gaussian HMMs with two hidden states are fitted for each index. The first uses that index's returns; the second additionally uses the previous common-observation returns of the other five indices. Means/regression coefficients and residual SD depend on the hidden state; transition probabilities are constant within each fitted model.</p>
<div class="math-display">$$x_{it}=100\log\frac{I_{it}}{I_{i,t-1}},\quad S_{it}^{(m)}\in\{0,1\},\quad \Pr(S_{it}^{(m)}=b\mid S_{i,t-1}^{(m)}=a)=A_{iab}^{(m)}.$$</div>
<div class="math-display">$$m=1:\quad x_{it}\mid S_{it}^{(1)}=s\sim\mathcal N(\mu_{is},\sigma_{is}^{2}),\\m=2:\quad x_{it}\mid S_{it}^{(2)}=s,\mathbf x_{-i,t-1}\sim\mathcal N\left(\beta_{is0}+\sum_{j\ne i}\beta_{isj}x_{j,t-1},\sigma_{is}^{2}\right).$$</div>
<p>I is the index close; x is the log return in percent; i and j identify indices; t identifies a common observation; m is the method; s is the latent state; A is a two-state transition matrix; μ is the state mean; β are state-specific regression coefficients; σ is residual SD. The state with larger σ is labelled stress. Stress can include large positive returns and does not mean every observation is a loss.</p>
<p>Six seeded initialisations are tried for each two-state full-history and training-only fit. Selection uses the highest finite likelihood among valid converged starts, not a desired regime frequency. Degenerate SD or a state with fewer than 20 posterior-weighted observations is rejected. The competing one-state model is fitted to the identical response and predictors. All twelve selected full-history fits converged.</p>
<div class="math-display">$$q_{it}^{(m)}=\Pr(S_{it}^{(m)}=1\mid x_{1:T}),\quad d_{it}^{(m)}=\mathbf1\{q_{it}^{(m)}>0.5\},\quad L_{it}=1+\frac{d_{it}^{(1)}+d_{it}^{(2)}}2.$$</div>
<p>These retrospective q values come from <code>depmixS4::forwardbackward()</code> smoothing. Thresholding posterior probabilities is not Viterbi path decoding. Filtered probabilities condition only on observations up to t; full-fit filtering still uses parameters estimated on the complete sample. Genuine held-out filtering below instead freezes all parameters at the training boundary.</p><details markdown="1"><summary><strong>Table 2.c. </details><details markdown="1" id="market-analysis-3"><summary><strong>2.3. Baltic local-market state</strong></summary>

<div class="math-display">$$L_t^B=\frac15\sum_{i\in\mathcal B}L_{it},\qquad b_t=\mathbf1\{L_t^B\ge1.3\}.$$</div><p>𝓑 contains the five requested Baltic indices. Each index receives weight 1/5 and each HMM method weight 1/2: at least three of the ten method–index stress votes trigger the local stress state. This is a weighted voting level, not a calibrated probability. Because the regional indices overlap in constituents, ten votes are not ten independent observations.</p><details markdown="1"><summary><strong>Figure 2.b. Baltic-index stress probabilities: own history and lagged market information</strong></summary>

<img loading="lazy" src="figures/market_analysis/baltic_hmm_probabilities.png?v=7940ff0a7d3f" alt="Baltic-index stress probabilities: own history and lagged market information">

</details><details markdown="1"><summary><strong>Figure 2.c. Aggregated local and global stress levels with the equity threshold</strong></summary>

<img loading="lazy" src="figures/market_analysis/market_aggregated_levels.png?v=e93e3686085d" alt="Aggregated local and global stress levels with the equity threshold">

</details>

</details><details markdown="1" id="market-analysis-4"><summary><strong>2.4. Global MSCI World state</strong></summary>

<div class="math-display">$$L_t^G=L_{\mathrm{MSCI},t},\qquad g_t=\mathbf1\{L_t^G\ge1.3\}.$$</div><p>The global signal uses MSCI World with the same two-method aggregation. Since its possible levels are 1, 1.5 and 2, either method voting stress is sufficient at threshold 1.3. Both regions are equity markets: the bond-specific threshold 1.5 from the systemic-risk paper is not mechanically relabelled as a global-equity rule. Threshold sensitivity is reported below.</p><details markdown="1"><summary><strong>Figure 2.d. MSCI World returns, inferred global stress and model probabilities</strong></summary>

<img loading="lazy" src="figures/market_analysis/global_hmm_probabilities.png?v=6afd527a7b5f" alt="MSCI World returns, inferred global stress and model probabilities">

</details>

</details><details markdown="1" id="market-analysis-5"><summary><strong>2.5. Four combined market regimes</strong></summary>

<div class="math-display">$$R_t=1+b_t+2g_t\in\{1,2,3,4\}.$$</div><p>The four states combine a local Baltic condition with a global MSCI World condition. This changes the economic interpretation of the original stock/bond split; it is not a claim that global equities behave like bonds.</p><details markdown="1" open><summary><strong>Table 2.e. </details><details markdown="1" id="market-analysis-6"><summary><strong>2.6. Markov transition matrix and regime characteristics</strong></summary>

<div class="math-display">$$\pi=\pi\widehat P,\quad\sum_i\pi_i=1,\quad\mathbb E[D_i]=\frac1{1-\widehat P_{ii}},\quad\mathbb E[T_i^+]=\frac1{\pi_i},\\m_{jj}=0,\quad m_{ij}=1+\sum_{k\ne j}\widehat P_{ik}m_{kj}\quad(i\ne j).$$</div><div class="math-display">$$N_{ij}=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\mathbf1\{R_t=i,R_{t+1}=j\},\qquad\widehat P_{ij}=\frac{N_{ij}}{\sum_kN_{ik}},\quad\sum_j\widehat P_{ij}=1.$$</div><p>Rows are the current regime and columns the next regime. All four states are represented; no transition row is fabricated. This joint matrix is estimated from the combined observed regime sequence, not from a Kronecker product assuming independent Baltic/global chains.</p><details markdown="1"><summary><strong>Table 2.g. </details><p><strong>Examples:</strong> R1 persistence is 96.29% per common observation; its model-implied mean spell is 26.97 steps. The fixed-matrix mean first passage R1→R4 is 124.81 steps; R4→R1 is 28.19. These are historical homogeneous-chain characteristics, not dates when a crisis or recovery must occur. Recurrence 1/π includes a return at the very next step when the state does not change; it is not the waiting time after leaving that state. The first-passage diagonal is zero, while recurrence is a separate quantity.</p><p>Higher persistence is useful when the regime is calm, but means longer stress when the regime is stressed. A higher model-implied R4 share means more frequent joint stress; a longer R1→R4 first-passage time means a longer model-implied wait for joint stress; a shorter R4→R1 time means faster return to calm. All such comparisons remain conditional on the fixed-matrix approximation.</p><details markdown="1"><summary><strong>Figure 2.g. Fixed-matrix regime probabilities at several horizons</strong></summary>

<img loading="lazy" src="figures/market_analysis/regime_horizon_probabilities.png?v=c129e1fa67ea" alt="Fixed-matrix regime probabilities at several horizons">

</details>

</details><details markdown="1" id="market-analysis-7"><summary><strong>2.7. Diagnostics, time variation and held-out validation</strong></summary>

<p><strong>First-order Markov check:</strong> conditional-on-label bootstrap p = 0.174. The first-order approximation is not rejected, which is not proof that aggregation of hidden chains is itself Markov.</p><p><strong>Time homogeneity is rejected:</strong> bootstrap p = 0.002. Transition patterns changed across the historical sample. The full-period matrix, stationary probabilities, first-passage times and fixed-P horizon curves are descriptive model characteristics, not validated invariant future probabilities. Recent-window estimates and historical blocks are provided to expose that change.</p><details markdown="1"><summary><strong>Table 2.k. Markov-property and time-homogeneity diagnostics</strong></summary>

Transition-matrix stress sensitivity</strong></summary>

<p>The stress-test adaptation multiplies worsening transitions 1→2, 1→3, 1→4, 2→4 and 3→4 by k, leaves other off-diagonal transitions unchanged, and adjusts each diagonal to preserve its row sum. Regimes 2 and 3 are not intrinsically ordered as better/worse than one another.</p><div class="math-display">$$P^{(k)}_{ij}=k\widehat P_{ij}\quad((i,j)\in\{(1,2),(1,3),(1,4),(2,4),(3,4)\}),\qquad P^{(k)}_{ii}=1-\sum_{j\ne i}P^{(k)}_{ij}.$$</div><details markdown="1"><summary><strong>Table 2.p. Artificial transition stress: admissibility, stationary shares and time to joint stress</strong></summary>

</details><p>Multipliers producing a negative diagonal are rejected, not clipped or renormalised into a different model. For these data k = 20 and 50 are inadmissible. This experiment perturbs a historical matrix; it is not an estimated probability of an actual future crisis and does not generate new portfolio trades.</p>

</details><details markdown="1" id="market-analysis-10"><summary><strong>2.10. Methodology sources and adaptation</strong></summary>

<p>The first paper motivates separate binary hidden states, a four-regime combination, transition estimates, stationary and first-passage characteristics, and worsening-transition stress tests. The second adds per-index own-history/market-conditioned estimation and weighted aggregation. Here stocks/bonds are replaced by Baltic/global equities, predictors are lagged, both equity thresholds are 1.3, and probabilities are explicitly posterior-threshold decoded. This implementation uses EM-fitted Gaussian HMMs in depmixS4; it does not implement the separate Lavielle–Lebarbier MCMC change-point procedure discussed in the first paper.</p><p><a href="https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10479-024-06041-1" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Stress testing for IInd pillar life-cycle pension funds using hidden Markov model</a>; <a href="https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13362-024-00144-x" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Systemic risk assessment through connectedness and spillover</a>; <a href="https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v036i07" target="_blank" rel="noopener">depmixS4 methods</a>; <a href="https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/markovchain/vignettes/an_introduction_to_markovchain_package.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener">markovchain methods</a>.</p>

</details></details><!-- MARKET_ANALYSIS_END -->

<details markdown="1">
<summary><strong>Figure 3.e. SSD pairwise dominance matrix used by netSD</strong></summary>

A blue cell equals 1 when the row entity SSD-dominates the column entity. Row sums contribute to OUT; column sums contribute to IN.

<a href="figures/netsd_reference_SSD_matrix.png?v=e026f7c697d2" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><img loading="lazy" src="figures/netsd_reference_SSD_matrix.png?v=e026f7c697d2" alt="SSD pairwise dominance matrix used by netSD"></a>

</details>

<details markdown="1">
<summary><strong>Figure 3.f. TSD pairwise dominance matrix used by netSD</strong></summary>

A blue cell equals 1 when the row entity TSD-dominates the column entity, including the required mean-return condition.

<a href="figures/netsd_reference_TSD_matrix.png?v=acf28debcf20" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><img loading="lazy" src="figures/netsd_reference_TSD_matrix.png?v=acf28debcf20" alt="TSD pairwise dominance matrix used by netSD"></a>

</details>

<details markdown="1">
<summary><strong>Figure 3.g. Combined FSD + SSD + TSD matrix used to calculate netSD</strong></summary>

Each cell is the sum of the three order-specific indicators and therefore ranges from 0 to 3. For every entity, OUT is its combined row sum and IN is its combined column sum. The frozen full-universe denominator is 175; netSD = (OUT − IN) / 175. The same reference matrix is used for all historical diagnostics; scenario outcomes additionally append the scenario week.

<a href="figures/netsd_reference_all_orders_matrix.png?v=4c003315d83e" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><img loading="lazy" src="figures/netsd_reference_all_orders_matrix.png?v=4c003315d83e" alt="Combined dominance matrix used to calculate netSD"></a>

</details>

The five-year average yield uses ex-dividend amounts divided by the latest available price on or before each ex-date. Current- and update-quantity dividend amounts use the five-year average annual dividend per share; they are historical gross scenarios, not forecasts.

allocation_change_direction describes the optimiser's target relative to current holdings. It is not the current execution recommendation; use current_execution_decision in the canonical trade table and interactive share profiles for that purpose.

Benchmark measures use exact-date pairs with S&amp;P 500 USD price returns; currency and dividend bases differ.</p><p>— means the native R function is undefined for this sample, insufficient observations, or a missing benchmark; hover the cell for the specific reason. HMM regimes are assigned only on exactly matching dates. Full and Last 126 retain all available return dates; regime columns omit dates without a common market label. Regime definitions use the full-history HMM fit and are descriptive, not an independent investment backtest.</p><p><strong>Path measures:</strong> drawdown, recovery and cumulative-return measures in regime columns use a synthetic sequence of the selected regime observations in chronological order, with other days omitted. They are not the actual drawdown or realised investment return across the omitted days. Annualisation uses 252 selected observations, not elapsed calendar time. Benchmark measures use exact-date pairs with S&amp;P 500 USD price returns; currency and dividend bases differ.</p><p>— means the native R function is undefined for this sample, insufficient observations, or a missing benchmark; hover the cell for the specific reason. Sparse regimes are labelled with their actual sample size.</p><table class="regime-performance"><thead><tr><th>Measure</th><th>Entire in-sample</th><th>Last 126</th><th>R1</th><th>R2</th><th>R3</th><th>R4</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><button type="button" class="metric-help-button" data-metric="ActiveReturn" data-meaning="Return above the benchmark." data-calculation="Rₚ − Rᵦ." data-interpretation="Higher is better.">ActiveReturn</button></td><td><span title="">0.097597</span></td><td><span title="">-0.027046</span></td><td><span title="">-0.034998</span></td><td><span title="">6.385585</span></td><td><span title="">0.669981</span></td><td><span title="Insufficient observations: 0 ; Benchmark measures use exact-date pairs with S&amp;P 500 USD price returns; currency and dividend bases differ.</p><p>— means the native R function is undefined for this sample, insufficient observations, or a missing benchmark; hover the cell for the specific reason. Regime definitions use the full-history HMM fit and are descriptive, not an independent investment backtest.</p><p><strong>Path measures:</strong> drawdown, recovery and cumulative-return measures in regime columns use a synthetic sequence of the selected regime observations in chronological order, with other days omitted. They are not the actual drawdown or realised investment return across the omitted days. Annualisation uses 252 selected observations, not elapsed calendar time. Benchmark measures use exact-date pairs with S&amp;P 500 USD price returns; currency and dividend bases differ.</p><p>— means the native R function is undefined for this sample, insufficient observations, or a missing benchmark; hover the cell for the specific reason. </table><details markdown="1" class=""><summary>All 72 PerformanceAnalytics measures: entire in-sample, last 126 and four regimes</summary><p>Reuses the existing cleaned price/NAV histories. HMM regimes are assigned only on exactly matching dates. Full and Last 126 retain all available return dates; regime columns omit dates without a common market label. Regime definitions use the full-history HMM fit and are descriptive, not an independent investment backtest.</p><p><strong>Path measures:</strong> drawdown, recovery and cumulative-return measures in regime columns use a synthetic sequence of the selected regime observations in chronological order, with other days omitted. They are not the actual drawdown or realised investment return across the omitted days. Annualisation uses 252 selected observations, not elapsed calendar time. Regime definitions use the full-history HMM fit and are descriptive, not an independent investment backtest.</p><p><strong>Path measures:</strong> drawdown, recovery and cumulative-return measures in regime columns use a synthetic sequence of the selected regime observations in chronological order, with other days omitted. They are not the actual drawdown or realised investment return across the omitted days. Annualisation uses 252 selected observations, not elapsed calendar time. Benchmark measures use exact-date pairs with S&amp;P 500 USD price returns; currency and dividend bases differ.</p><p>— means the native R function is undefined for this sample, insufficient observations, or a missing benchmark; hover the cell for the specific reason. HMM regimes are assigned only on exactly matching dates. Full and Last 126 retain all available return dates; regime columns omit dates without a common market label. Regime definitions use the full-history HMM fit and are descriptive, not an independent investment backtest.</p><p><strong>Path measures:</strong> drawdown, recovery and cumulative-return measures in regime columns use a synthetic sequence of the selected regime observations in chronological order, with other days omitted. They are not the actual drawdown or realised investment return across the omitted days. Annualisation uses 252 selected observations, not elapsed calendar time. Benchmark measures use exact-date pairs with S&amp;P 500 USD price returns; currency and dividend bases differ.</p><p>— means the native R function is undefined for this sample, insufficient observations, or a missing benchmark; hover the cell for the specific reason. Benchmark measures use exact-date pairs with S&amp;P 500 USD price returns; currency and dividend bases differ.</p><p>— means the native R function is undefined for this sample, insufficient observations, or a missing benchmark; hover the cell for the specific reason.
